summary: State-built 60-foot steel lookout near Colfax, erected in 1930 after a county funding dispute; a 2024 trip report found it closed behind a locked gate.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab, an Aermotor Company product; a house on the grounds was built under the ECW program in 1935
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Nevada-Yuba-Placer Unit (Cal Fire NEU)

access.note: A 2024 trip report found the facility closed, with a locked gate at the junction with Mt. Howell Rd

visit.trail_note: Do not pass the locked gate. Check with Cal Fire before planning any visit.

events.note: Erected by the State in 1930 as the Mt. Howell Lookout Station on the McDonald ranch near Landers Station. Lions clubs and residents donated time and money for the access road.
Ed Hinchey of Colfax was to be in charge of the station after June 1, 1930
A November 1930 notice said the Landers Lookout station would close for the winter. Whether that is this tower is not confirmed.
House on the grounds built under the Emergency Conservation Work program; the register says it still reflects its CCC origin
Cab modification and catwalk addition, circa 1957
A 2024 trip report found the facility closed behind a locked gate, with buildings near the tower boarded up

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls it Howell Hill Lookout. The 1930 press called it the Mt. Howell Lookout Station. The story uses both names.
A November 1930 notice names a Landers Lookout station that closed for the winter. The sources do not confirm whether it is this tower, and the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'standing' kept. The only 2024 evidence is one hiker's trip report, a single witness. The Placer County lookout page (placer.ca.gov) returned 403, so no official Cal Fire or county page was read. A search summary said Placer County Fire operates the tower; that is unverified and left out. The register lists Cal Fire NEU as the administrator. The 1927-30 newspaper items are read through the Forest Lookouts page's transcriptions, not the original papers. The trip report's remark that visiting on foot seems fine is not endorsed in the story. The trip report places the concrete footings on Camels Hump, a different summit in the same report, not on Howell Hill; the story says so. The brief had no height; 60 feet from the register. No photos added; the register credits a June 3, 1930 Stockton Independent photo but gives no image URL.
